title: Fix tenant metric shadowing and trace discontinuities after failover causing missing console widgets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer escalation from a large Dedicated tenant reported intermittent disappearance of per-tenant dashboards and opaque gaps in traces during a regional failover window. Impact included missing SLA slices in the Console, alerts firing with no visible metric timeseries, and user-reported inability to correlate traces to metric spikes. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and permanent fix for the component that is shadowing tenant metrics and dropping trace link metadata during high-throughput failover/autoscale scenarios.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate regional failover by draining a dedicated pool (use infra playbook). 2) Replay production-like traffic using load harness (locust job: loadtests/tenant-heavy.yaml). 3) Observe per-tenant metrics in metrics-ingest; check console widget rendering for tenant X. 4) Query traces service for span IDs referenced in the metric pipeline. 5) Intermittently, metrics appear with zeroed tenant_id or are queued into the global fallback buffer causing dashboards to show 'no data'.
observed_behavior: - Metrics for affected tenants either vanish from the Console or appear with a generic tenant id 't-unknown'. - Traces are ingested but trace -> metric linking metadata (trace_id -> metric labels) is missing on a portion of requests. - Alerts triggered but console panels show empty series. - Issue reproduces reliably under simulated failover and burst traffic.
hypothesis_root_cause: During failover/autoscale, the metric router can atomically switch to a fallback ingestion path. A race condition in the router's tenant-context propagation causes tenant_id to be cleared for batches that cross node boundaries. Additionally, a GC/tombstone policy in the trace-link cache prematurely evicts keys when eviction heuristics mis-evaluate bursty TTLs, causing traces to lack the metric linkage.
proposed_solution: 1) Patch metric-router to preserve tenant context across batch boundary transitions and add an explicit tenant_id tag at the start of each batch. 2) Harden trace-link cache: extend TTL for candidate keys during failover windows and change eviction policy to LRU-with-guard to avoid premature tombstoning. 3) Add end-to-end invariant checks: a debug header that asserts tenant_id presence and emits a one-off audit log when missing. 4) Deploy as canary to a single Dedicated region, run smoke tests, then ramp.
work_items: - ENG-59113: unit tests and integration harness for tenant propagation. - ENG-59114: cache eviction policy change and stress test. - ENG-59115: console panel guard and clearer missing-data message. - ENG-59116: runbook update and customer communication draft.
test_plan: - Run integration harness with tenant traffic and verify no 't-unknown' tags. - End-to-end: generate a synthetic trace and ensure metric->trace linkage exists within 30s. - Load test at 3x normal failover throughput and verify no missing panels for 10 consecutive runs. - Canary run in dedicated-region-2 for 48 hours with elevated telemetry sampling.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs and build image. 2) Canary to dedicated-region-2 (5% of tenant traffic) for 48h. 3) If telemetry checks pass, ramp to remaining dedicated regions over 24h. 4) Hosted region patch deployed after Dedicated canaries. 5) Private deployments: provide patch bundle and upgrade notes to solutions team.
rollback_plan: Revert metric-router and cache changes via deployment rollback; remove canary tag. If rollback insufficient, toggle 'preserve-tenant-context' feature flag to false which restores pre-change routing behavior while retaining cache guard adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: - No 't-unknown' events in metrics pipeline for 72h post-ramp. - Trace->metric linkage success rate >= 99.9% under failover load tests. - Customer confirms dashboards restored and no further escalations. - Post-deploy metrics show no increase in latency >5%.
